# the contributor proof audit: four bounded mechanisms

These audits concern the named auxiliary results only. None is an
arbitrary-source proof of OC, and the active goal is not complete.

## Exact contained additions and anchor credit: PASS

Read candidate 1d1be0b22c707856 and
candidate 8e66c09047f42ba1 in full.
The profile minimum is positive by the proved equality classification
for simplex centroid caps; its reflected threshold remains a genuine
tail even at support levels. The d=2 minimum is exactly
2(sqrt(10)-3)/9. The paired thresholds belong to one original ambient
cap, so the proof includes arbitrary integer-continuous coupling.

For multiple owned additions, either all are captured or one opposite
core partner pays the reflected-tail threshold. Hence no partner mass
is double counted. The vertical estimate is valid since
Gamma_d+rho_d<2Gamma_d<1 for d>=2. The one-extra d=1 and centrally
symmetric calibrations use reflection separately.

The integer projection with a common anchor is exactly the cube and the
selected negative binary points: an outside -1 coordinate first removes
all cube vertices from a convex representation, and remaining binary
extremality forces one selected point. Checked the explicit exposing
functional signs, the finite isolating coefficients, and uniqueness.

The LP's Farkas signs and the finite minimum defining chi are correct.
Its upper bounds apply to every core point using a barycentric coordinate
at least 1/(d+1). A zero-volume fiber lies outside the convex hull of
positive-volume bases, since positive Minkowski interpolation otherwise
gives positive fiber volume; it therefore has depth zero. This justifies
the global bracket's handling of such fibers.

The six-base triangle contains exactly the claimed six integers. Its
two opposite small fibers have identical centroid g, so the proved
paired-centroid-tail bound gives their 2Gamma_d a payment. The matching
canonical caps keep the two adjacent core traces at supporting levels
of zero d-volume. The other anchor isolations and the finite upper cover
give global maximum Gamma_d V+a only in the stated small-a regime.
The nonanchor LP discrepancy is a first-order partial-trace obstruction,
not a counterexample to OC or to the displayed upper bound.

The one-extra verifier passed 101 profile, 5304 coupled-cap and 33537
isolation checks. The multiple-addition verifier is separately recorded
by its author; the proofs above do not rely on its finite screens.

## Fixed-normal transport and sharp parity loss: PASS

Read fixed-normal-cap-transport-collisions-and-sharp-parity-loss.md.
The lexicographic monotone coupling has distinct midpoint targets within
each parity. Different parities require a target-wise maximum, not a sum.
The two target lower bounds and the collision loss identity retain that
distinction. Missing high-threshold parity traces cannot contribute the
usual positive-positive Phi expression.

The actual simplex C_N and fixed oblique normal z_1+x_1 have the claimed
whole-fiber cap traces at integer thresholds, since 0<=x_1<=1/2. Unit
cube integration gives the two exact polynomial bounds on U_N. The
chosen t leaves a positive tail in every parity. The resulting ratio is
squeezed to 2^{-n}; no halfspace normal varies with the sequence. The
two-adjacent-fiber example correctly shows that combining parities before
applying Phi can lose every positive comparison constant. The exact
verifier passed 15577 checks.

## Angular cancellation and the conditioned bridge: PASS

Read private-cone-radial-balancing-obstruction-and-angular-window-bridge.md.
Independently checked the rectangle private areas, overlap, cyclic
determinant-one matrix, and the exact actual three-base projection.
The common section is interior to every real fiber. Equal-height source
pieces have mass L/4 but all permitted midpoints lie in an area-1/4
rectangle. Thus the claimed density-at-most-one obstruction is valid.

The positive angular slack and common height window give both midpoint
margin inequalities directly; all other margins are nonpositive. Distinct
unordered pair regions are disjoint except on zero-volume hyperplanes.
The max-over-parity qualification and exact homothety Jacobians are
essential and correctly stated. No lower bound for the fraction of source
mass satisfying a common positive slack is claimed. Exact verifier passed
10716 checks.

## Shape distance under vertex truncation: PASS

Read volume-preserving-simplex-truncation-obstructs-low-order-coercivity.md.
The restored-volume body's inner deletion and outer shell both have mass
delta V, proving its exact TV and halfspace-cap distances. The displayed
centroid displacement bound follows from alpha-1<=delta/d and alpha<2.

In the all-affine-simplex Hausdorff proof, distinct support vertices near
e_i are forced by coordinate maxima. The remaining vertex must maximize
all d lower-corner exposing functionals; summing their inequalities gives
exactly (d-1)epsilon/[2d(2d-1)]. The contradiction uses epsilon<=1/d as
stated. No approximating minimizer is assumed. The Banach--Mazur sandwich
has Hausdorff error at most lambda-1 because its inner simplex has diameter
at most one. Checked the centroid homothet's matching upper order and the
fixed-neighbor source's strict middle inclusion. The obstruction is to
exponents p<d in geometric shape distance; it makes no claim ruling out
linear cap-distance stability or an exponent-d shape modulus.

The new root exact truncated-simplex law strengthens this example's
upper rate to the asymptotic equality
depth-Gamma_d=(Gamma_d-1/(d+1))epsilon^d+O(epsilon^{2d}); that separate
all-direction theorem is undergoing independent audit.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
